## Bug Fixes

- **Yes, clear context and implement** now hands the full approved plan to the fresh session and keeps the current session open if the handoff fails. (#60763)

## Desktop

### Improvements
- OpenCode 1 now offers the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0. OpenCode 2 downloads in the background and installs only when you choose: Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later. Your sessions, projects, and settings are kept. Plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update.

## Core

### Bugfixes
- Sessions with many images no longer send oversized requests. When the images in a session's history pass 25 MiB, the oldest are replaced with a placeholder.
- A provider error for a request body that is too large now starts compaction and a retry instead of failing the turn.

### New Features

- **Fork sessions whose folder is gone**: when a session's original folder was moved or deleted, you can now fork it into the current folder instead of only continuing, so later resumes no longer ask. See [Continue or switch sessions](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.2/packages/coding-agent/docs/sessions.md#continue-or-switch-sessions).

### Changed

- When a session's working directory no longer exists, for example after the project folder was renamed, interactive mode now offers `Continue`, `Fork`, or `Cancel` instead of only continuing. `Continue` runs the session in the current directory without storing the choice, as before; `Fork` copies it into the current directory as a new session with a new ID, like `--fork`, so the next resume no longer asks. This applies at startup (`--session`, `--resume`), to `/resume`, to `/import`, and to `ctx.switchSession()` from extensions ([#11975](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), fixes [#11060](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))

### Fixed

- Fixed `/import` of a session whose working directory no longer exists leaving a copy in the session directory, and continuing it leaving a second copy with the same ID (`s.jsonl` and `s-1.jsonl`); the failed copy is now removed ([#11975](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), fixes [#11060](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))

# Skill toggles, tool timers and a faster Hyper ⚡ This release was brought to you by our team and our favorite contributors! Long awaited features ahead, read along! ## Toggle skills Skills can now be switched on and off right from the command palette. Broken skills are easy to spot, too! (they're marked with a red × and the reason they failed) ## 🕐 How long is this taking? Every tool call now shows how long it's been running. Now, you'll know whether that test suite is just slow or actually stuck. ## Lighter, faster Hyper ⚡ Requests to Hyper are now compressed with [Brotli](https://brotli.org/) 🥦. That means much smaller uploads on every turn and snappier responses, especially in long sessions. Hyper now also supports [Gzip](https://www.gzip.org/) that other agents could use when Brotli if not viable. Big thanks to @BrunoKrugel for the first 2 awesome features! ## Most of AutoCua now runs in Rust

Since 0.2.0 most of the agent code has moved from Python to Rust. Rust is now the largest language in the repository (about 45%, up from 23% in 0.2.0). It still ships prebuilt in the wheel, so you never need Rust. Each part was compared with the Python it replaced, case by case, before the switch.

- **Computer use:** one Rust agent now runs on macOS, Windows and Linux in place of three Python agents. Each system keeps its own prompts. Windows picks up what its copy had fallen behind on, such as the "Pure vision first" hint and the newer URL finder for site skills.
- **iPhone agent:** the agent, its controller (taps, typing, scrolls, opening apps, the shell, the video player, notes and the todo list) and its tool registry.
- **LLM layer:** the manager every agent sends its requests through, the Responses route and all eleven model providers.
- **Shared tools:** web search, the shell, the browser sub-agent and the Android sub-agent are now one copy each for every system, in `AutoCua/universal_tool`. They replace six copies of the web tool and fifteen copies of the others.
- **Also in Rust:** the tool registries, notes and todo lists for macOS, Windows and Linux, the vault, memory compression and the app's chat memory.
- The shell tools of computer use and the iPhone agent now run in the coder's sandbox. The old Python sandboxes are gone.
- The screen and phone readers, the desktop controllers and the app itself are still Python.

The version jumps from 0.2.0 to 3.0.0 to mark this move. There is no 1.x or 2.x.

## New provide

`pip install 'browser-use==1.0.6'`

- **BU 4.0 is the default model.** `Agent(task)` and `ChatBrowserUse()` now run `bu-4.0` on the Browser Use gateway instead of `bu-fast`. Pass `llm='bu-4.0-mini'` for simple tasks at the lowest cost, or `llm='bu-4.0-pro'` for the hardest tasks (#6430).
- **This costs more if you pass no `llm`.** BU 4.0 tokens cost 15 times as much as `bu-fast` ($1.80 / $9.00 per 1M input / output tokens, against $0.12 / $0.60), and it runs at high instead of medium reasoning in the default mode. A short test task cost $0.022 instead of $0.0014. To keep the previous model and price, pass `llm='bu-fast'`. Prices: https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/models
- The first run without a key opens Browser Use login and continues after approval; cloud browsers print their live-view link (#6425).
- Judge gotchas stay grounded in what the run observed (#6418).

## Highlights

### Resumable Agent streams (now for every Agent)
Every `Agent` can now publish a resumable run stream with replay caching, cross-instance observe/abort (`agent.observe(runId)`, `observe().abort()`, `agent.abortRunStream(runId)`), and ownership/TTL enforcement—so clients can reconnect without killing the run by default.

### Built-in MCP server at `/api/mcp` + OAuth discovery
`@mastra/server` now ships a built-in MCP endpoint (enabled by default when `server.auth` is configured) so MCP clients can call your agents/workflows/tools without defining an `MCPServer`, plus OAuth discovery/audience checks via `server.mcp.oauth` and a new introspection route `GET /api/mcp/builtin`.

### Workflow Storage Version 2 (delta writes) now supported on Postgres + libSQL
Experimental `storageVersion: 2` reduces writes by persisting only per-step changes (instead of rewriting the whole run) and now works with `@mastra/pg` and `@mastra/libsql`, with results that can lazily load step history via an async `steps()` function.

### Resumable AI SDK chat routes (`useChat({ resume: true })` support)
`chatRoute({ resumable: true })` now generates a POST + reconnect GET endpoint pair that replays/follows active runs via `agent.observe(runId)`, with explicit route-array configuration support (`server.apiRoutes: [routes]`).

### One-off and bounded schedules for agents & workflows
Schedules now support one-time execution (`runAt`) and bounded recurring execution (`endAt`), with TypeScript updates (`cron` is optional) across server, client, and multiple storage backends.

### Highlights

-   **Pi 1.5 support:** `agents/harness/pi`, `agents/models/pi-ai` and the Pi tools now run on Pi 1.5.
-   **Far fewer storage writes while streaming:** Pi stores streamed answers and tool output in batches, at the latest every second, instead of on every update. Over SQLite this cuts storage transactions about 27x for long answers and 5.7x for turns with parallel tools, and CPU by about a quarter. A crash can now lose up to about a second of streamed output.
-   **Faster with many sessions:** Pi's scheduler no longer rechecks every conversation on each commit, so on SQLite one Pi harness with 2,048 sessions went from 88 to 459 agent runs per second. Commits that arrive together now share one storage call, and a normal run makes no storage reads.
-   **Large answers no longer blow up memory:** streaming a 500 KB tool call used to take about 20 s of CPU and a 100 MB heap, and a 140 KB answer followed by a 140 KB tool call held over 100 MB. Pi now appends new text instead of copying it on every update.
-   **Conversation view:** `session.watch()` replaces `session.events()`. It returns the newest transcript entries and the session's live state, such as the answer being streamed, running tools, and why the last run ended without an answer. `session.entries()` pages older entries. ## Security fix

With the ReAct runner (`runner: react`), `ReactConverter` fell back to Python `eval()` on the model's `Action:` text whenever it was not valid JSON. A prompt-injected action (from a web page, tool result or document the agent reads) could execute arbitrary Python on the host. Actions are now parsed with `ast.literal_eval` and must be a dict with `name` and `arguments`. Reported through TSRC.

The default `openai` runner is not affected. Upgrade if you use the ReAct runner.
